summary: A chair-supported one-leg toe stand from the NIA older-adult guide, following its progression from the two-leg version.

muscleRoles.qualifier: Qualitative connection between plantar flexion and historical anatomy; no activation percentage or head isolation is established.
Qualitative connection between plantar flexion and historical anatomy; no activation percentage or head isolation is established.

setup: Hold a sturdy chair for balance; begin from the supported toe-stand position.
Use one leg at a time as described in the source progression.
executionSteps: Breathe out while slowly lifting the working heel to rise onto the toes.
Hold for 1 second, then breathe in while lowering slowly.
Repeat on the other leg while retaining chair support.
technique.finishOrReset: Lower the heel slowly to the floor.
keyCheckpoints: Keep the sturdy support available and move slowly.

mistakes.mistake: Moving abruptly or removing the stated chair support.
mistakes.whyItMatters: This differs from the supported source version.
mistakes.correction: Retain sturdy support and use slow, controlled movement.

programmingGuidance.qualifier: Printed page 62 gives a one-leg progression totaling 10–15 repetitions per leg. It gives no separate set count or timed rest for that progression; the two-leg two-set prescription is not transferred. Older-adult education, not a universal training dose.

stopSignals: Stop for chest pain or pressure, severe joint pain, dizziness or feeling unwell.
safety.notes: NIA older-adult safety context: seek qualified advice when unsure about suitability, after surgery or with health concerns. This page provides no individual medical clearance.
